# Design Document ## Overview One GitHub Actions workflow, one `version.json`, one new unary RPC, one line under the login form, one ZIP per merged build. The design's center of gravity is **reusing what already exists**: the gates are the four commands CLAUDE.md already defines, the version authority is the assembly NB.GV already stamps, the pre-auth wire is the interceptor exception `Login` already uses, and the ZIP's shape is the production hosting mode `MapClientApp` already implements (static files + `index.html` fallback when `Client:DevServerUrl` is empty). ## Steering Document Alignment ### Technical Standards (tech.md) - **gRPC call shapes**: the version travels as one unary call on an existing service — no new stream, no REST side-channel beside the gRPC surface the client already speaks. - **One source of truth**: the version is computed by NB.GV from git history; the backend reads its own stamped assembly; the client asks the backend. Nothing stores a second copy. - **Commands rule**: untouched — this spec changes no document-editing path. ### Project Structure (structure.md) - The workflow lives at `.github/workflows/build.yml`; `version.json` at the repository root; the backend pieces in their existing areas (`Sessions/` for the interceptor change, the service registration where `AuthenticationService` already lives); the client pieces in `src/client/src/pages/` and `src/client/src/index.css`. ## Code Reuse Analysis ### Existing Components to Leverage - **`SessionInterceptor`** (`src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend/Sessions/SessionInterceptor.cs`): already exempts `/Login` from the session-token requirement; `DescribeProduct` joins that exemption the same way. - **`AuthenticationService`** (`src/api/authentication.proto` + its backend implementation): gains the `DescribeProduct` rpc — the one service the login page already talks to before any session exists. - **`MapClientApp` production mode**: serves `wwwroot` statics with an `index.html` fallback when `Client:DevServerUrl` is empty. The ZIP is exactly a `dotnet publish` output whose `wwwroot` holds the client's production build; no hosting code changes. - **`Directory.Build.props` / `Directory.Packages.props`** (`src/`): the central place the NB.GV package reference and version land, so every C# project is stamped without per-project edits. - **The gates themselves**: the workflow runs the same four commands CLAUDE.md names, verbatim, from the same directories. - **`buf`**: already an npm devDependency; `npm ci` at `src/` provides it — the workflow installs no extra tooling for codegen. ### Integration Points - **NB.GV → assemblies**: `Nerdbank.GitVersioning` referenced once in `src/Directory.Build.props` (version pinned centrally, `PrivateAssets="all"`); it stamps `AssemblyInformationalVersion` (semver + git height + commit id) on every build, local or CI. - **NB.GV → workflow**: the `nbgv` CLI (`dotnet tool`) reads the same `version.json` to name the tag and the ZIP, so the workflow and the assemblies cannot disagree. - **Backend → client**: `DescribeProduct` returns the backend's own `AssemblyInformationalVersion`. The login page calls it on mount over the existing transport and renders the line, or omits it on failure (Requirement 3.3). ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR G[git history + version.json] -->|NB.GV MSBuild| ASM[stamped assemblies] G -->|nbgv CLI| WF[workflow: tag + ZIP name] ASM -->|AssemblyInformationalVersion| RPC[AuthenticationService.DescribeProduct] RPC -->|unary, pre-auth| LP[LoginPage version line] WF -->|gh release create| REL[GitHub Release + ZIP] ASM --> PUB[dotnet publish + client dist as wwwroot] PUB --> REL ``` ### The workflow (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) Triggers: `push` to `develop`, and `pull_request` targeting it. One job for the gates; a second, `develop`-push-only job for the release, needing the first. **Gate job** (ubuntu-latest — the line-ending policy lives in `.gitattributes`, so the CRLF-sensitive fixtures behave identically there): 1. `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` — NB.GV needs the full history to compute height; a shallow clone is the classic silent-wrong-version mistake. 2. `actions/setup-dotnet` (.NET 10, honouring `src/global.json`) and `actions/setup-node`, with NuGet and npm caching keyed on the lock/props files. 3. `npm ci` at `src/`. 4. The four gates, each its own step, each judged by its exit code, in the exact local form: `dotnet test --solution EtAlii.Adp.slnx` and `dotnet format style --verify-no-changes --severity info` from `src/backend`; `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` from `src/client`. No output grepping anywhere; the zero-test exit 5 fails the job as the broken build it is. 5. No automatic retries. The known teardown file-lock flakes are Windows-specific (`FileSystemWatcher` handle latency); if they reproduce on Linux the failure is visible and the hardening work is the fix — a blanket retry hiding real failures is explicitly not part of this design. **Release job** (only on `push` to `develop`, `permissions: contents: write`, the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` only): 1. `nbgv get-version` yields the semver (`$V`) and the cloud-build variables. 2. Guard: if tag `v$V` already exists (`gh release view v$V` / `git ls-remote --tags`), **fail loudly** — a published asset is never overwritten (Requirement 4.5). 3. `npm run build` in `src/client` (Vite production build to `dist/`). 4. `dotnet publish src/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Backend.Service -c Release -o publish/` — **framework-dependent, platform-neutral**: one ZIP for every OS, at the price of requiring the .NET 10 runtime on the target machine. Chosen over per-OS self-contained ZIPs because one artifact is honest about what this is (a first release pipeline) and the runtime prerequisite is one readme line; going self-contained later is additive. 5. Copy `src/client/dist/` into `publish/wwwroot/` — the exact layout `MapClientApp`'s production branch serves. 6. Write `publish/readme.md`: the version, the commit id, and how to run (`dotnet EtAlii.Adp.Backend.Service.dll`, requires the .NET 10 runtime, then browse to the listening address; the packaged `appsettings.json` must leave `Client:DevServerUrl` empty so static hosting engages). 7. Zip as `EtAlii.Adp-$V.zip`; `gh release create v$V` with the ZIP attached and generated notes. `gh` is preinstalled on runners — no third-party release action, no extra supply chain. ### Versioning (`version.json`) At the repository root: `{ "version": "0.1-alpha", "publicReleaseRefSpec": ["^refs/heads/develop$"] }` (initial number the maintainer's call at implementation time). `develop` is the public-release ref, so merged builds carry a clean semver while branch/PR builds carry NB.GV's prerelease marker — which is exactly Requirement 2.4's honest local version. The NB.GV package reference goes in `src/Directory.Build.props` with its version in `Directory.Packages.props`. ### The version wire (`DescribeProduct`) ```proto // authentication.proto - the one pre-auth service, so the login page can ask before any session exists. rpc DescribeProduct(DescribeProductRequest) returns (DescribeProductResponse); message DescribeProductRequest {} message DescribeProductResponse { string version = 1; // AssemblyInformationalVersion: semver+height, commit id embedded } ``` Backend: the handler reads `Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly()`'s `AssemblyInformationalVersionAttribute` once and caches it. `SessionInterceptor` exempts `/DescribeProduct` beside `/Login`, with the comment saying why (a version is not a secret, and the page that shows it exists before login). Considered and rejected: build-time injection into the client bundle (a second version copy that can drift from the backend actually running, and `nbgv` on every dev's npm path for nothing) and extending `LoginResponse` (the version must show *before* a login is submitted). ### The login page line `LoginPage.tsx` calls `describeProduct` on mount (fire-and-forget into state) and renders below the `auth-card` form: ```tsx {version !== "" &&

{version}

} ``` `.auth-version` joins the page's existing styles: centered, `--color-text-muted`, small — the centralized variables, no literal colors (the shell's convention, and small-refinements R3.4's rule). Failure or an empty answer renders nothing (Requirement 3.3). ### CLAUDE.md The two "there is no CI here" passages (backend code style, running the tests) are reworded: the gates are now also enforced by `.github/workflows/build.yml`; the local discipline (worktrees gate before merging) stands, with CI as the net under it. The exit-code lesson stays, now pointing at the workflow as its embodiment. ## Data Models No stored data. `DescribeProductResponse.version` is the one new wire field; `version.json` is the one new configuration file. ## Error Handling ### Error Scenarios 1. **Shallow clone in CI** → NB.GV fails the build with its own explicit error rather than computing a wrong height; `fetch-depth: 0` prevents it, and the failure mode is loud, not silent. 2. **Re-run of a published commit** → the tag-exists guard fails the release job with a message naming the existing release; the gate job's result stands. 3. **`DescribeProduct` unavailable** (dev client against a dead backend) → the login page renders no version line; no stale or invented number (Requirement 3.3). 4. **A gate flake on the runner** → the job fails and says which step; re-running is a human's visible action on the Actions page, never the workflow's own hidden loop. 5. **Zero tests discovered** → exit code 5 fails the gate step; the step's name tells the reader to suspect the build, not the suite, per the repository's recorded lesson. ## Testing Strategy ### Unit Testing - Backend: a test for the `DescribeProduct` handler (returns a non-empty version matching the informational-version shape); a `SessionInterceptor` test pinning that `/DescribeProduct` passes without a token while other calls still refuse. - Client: a `LoginPage` test with the call mocked — version shown when answered, nothing rendered when it fails. ### Integration Testing - The existing `WebApplicationFactory` harness gains one fact: an unauthenticated channel calls `DescribeProduct` and gets a version — proving the exemption end-to-end. - The workflow itself is validated by its first runs on a branch and PR: the design treats the first red/green cycle on GitHub as the integration test, since no local harness can execute Actions. ### End-to-End Testing - A `tests.md` entry: download the release ZIP, unzip, `dotnet EtAlii.Adp.Backend.Service.dll`, browse, and read the same version below the login panel as the release tag carries — the four-places-one-number check (Non-Functional Usability), which only a human with the artifact can perform.
